question: A company plans to deploy a Cisco HyperFlex solution for data-intensive applications and databases. The proposed solution should offer the highest performance with high consistency and low latency. Which Cisco HyperFlex storage configuration should be used?
theory: For data-intensive, database-style workloads that demand the highest performance with high consistency and the lowest possible latency, Cisco HyperFlex All-NVMe nodes are the right storage configuration, because NVMe drives connect directly to the CPU (bypassing the latency-adding PCIe switch/SAS controller path used by SATA/SAS SSDs), delivering more predictable, lower-latency I/O than Hybrid, All-Flash (SATA/SAS SSD), or All-HDD configurations. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 15 — HyperFlex All-NVMe Nodes)
